summary: Steel tower and towerman's cabin erected at Stuart Lake, Saskatchewan, in 1957-58; a towermen list gives Sandra Muench for 1998-2002, then 'went to aerial detection'.

facts.design: heavy steel tower with a towerman's cabin
facts.status_note: No source found says whether the tower still stands.

staffing.status: Sandra Muench listed for 1998 to 2002; the list then notes the tower went to aerial detection

facts.agency: Saskatchewan Department of Natural Resources (as named in the 1958 annual report)

events.note: Annual report for the year ending 31 March 1958, quoted on Canada Lookouts, says one steel tower and a towerman's cabin were erected at Stuart Lake.
Sandra Muench listed for 1998 to 2002 on the towermen list.
Last year of the 1998-2002 entry; the entry then notes the tower went to aerial detection.

sources.title: Firetowers of Saskatchewan: Firetowermen and Women

notes_for_editor: Thin record. Three pages give the build entry, a towermen list entry and a tower list entry; no source gives a status, access level or fate beyond 'went to aerial detection'. The firelookout.ca record is script-rendered and could not be read, so the brief's unknown status and access stand. The brief's agency (Saskatchewan Public Safety Agency) is not named in any fetched page; the story uses the Department of Natural Resources name from the 1958 report. The brief's other name 'Stewart' is not used: the Saskatchewan index lists a separate STEWART entry and Jim Settee's account names a different Stewart Tower. Two web searches returned nothing on the tower's current state.
